original_question: Characterize the representing measures for the origin in the unit ball in C^n .
target_in_paper: Closest problem-list target in arXiv:math/9509202: characterize the representing measures for the origin for the ball algebra on the unit ball in \u2102^n.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient domain (the unit ball in \u2102^n), the distinguished point (the origin), and the core task (to characterize representing measures).
missing_details: The relevant function algebra must be named: the ball algebra A(B_n), equivalently P(S), the uniform closure on the boundary sphere of holomorphic polynomials.
The unit ball should be defined explicitly as B_n = {z \in \u2102^n : \|z\| < 1}.
The measures are not arbitrary; they are Borel probability measures.
The support space should be specified as the boundary sphere S = \u2202B_n, not the open ball itself.
The origin is being viewed as the point-evaluation character f \mapsto f(0) on A(B_n).
The representing property must be stated explicitly: f(0) = \int_S f\,d\mu for every f \in A(B_n).
Equivalently, because A(B_n) is the uniform closure of holomorphic polynomials on S, one may quantify over all holomorphic polynomials p instead of all f \in A(B_n).
To keep the several-complex-variables setting faithful, one should state n \ge 2 rather than leave the one-variable disk-algebra case mixed in.
The word 'characterize' should be understood as giving necessary and sufficient conditions for exactly which measures \mu belong to the convex set of representing measures for 0.
refined_question: Let B_n = {z \in \u2102^n : \|z\| < 1} with n \ge 2, let S = \u2202B_n, and let A(B_n) = P(S) denote the ball algebra, i.e. the uniform closure on S of the holomorphic polynomials. Characterize all Borel probability measures \mu on S that represent evaluation at the origin, in the sense that f(0) = \int_S f\,d\mu for every f \in A(B_n).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, describe the convex set M_0(S) = {\mu \in \operatorname{Prob}(S) : \int_S p\,d\mu = p(0) \text{ for every holomorphic polynomial } p}.
justification: arXiv:math/9509202 is a problem list rather than a theorem/proposition paper, so the nearest paper-faithful target is the corresponding open problem itself. Your draft is close in spirit, but it leaves the phrase 'representing measures' underdetermined: in this setting one must specify the ball algebra, the boundary sphere on which the measures live, the probability condition, and the exact integral identity that represents the point-evaluation functional at 0. The standard nearby ball-algebra formulation is the one used in the auxiliary sources cited below, which make explicit the notation B_n, S = \u2202B_n, A(B_n) = P(S), and M_0(S).
